content.comment_body: Hello, I have a turbine cold water meter with a pulse transmitter that I want to connect to a [product_name] ([article_no]) for pulse counting purposes. The water meter features open collector type outputs (OD) [0.17A, 100V]. My question is: how do I connect these open collector outputs to digital inputs on the [product_name]? Is it possible to connect as shown in the attached diagram?

Open collector refers to connecting the positive side of the power supply to a resistor of around 5KOhm to 10KOhm. Connect the other end of the resistor to the desired digital input, such as I1, and link that digital input to the output of the pulse sensor. Also, connect the power supply negative to the negative of the pulse sensor. Keep in mind, the input signal will be inverted.
Did I interpret your instructions correctly? (refer to attached photo)
Would it be better to use an additional device for this setup?

You understood correctly, and as long as both parts share the same ground (M), using a photo coupler is not necessary. If you encounter voltage issues at the [product_name] input, you can lower the resistor value to 2.2kOhm. Regards, [user_name]
If you use input I2 as shown in your diagram, you'll need a resistor for I2 as well.
I'm not a fan of using resistors since it doesn't look clean. I'll try using a solid-state relay module - PLC-OSC- 24DC/ 24DC/ 2 - [article_no]. [url]

It's your choice whether to buy photo couplers with built-in resistors, or use resistors on their own. Alternatively, you could purchase ready-made resistor terminals or resistor arrays for DIN rails, also available from Phoenix, but the decision is yours. If you wire the photo coupler as shown in your diagram, it won't work. Terminal 13 (+) should be connected to 24V, and terminal 14 to the input. Good luck.
